ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Airway opening without trauma

A 52-year-old is unresponsive after a witnessed nontraumatic collapse. Snoring improves when the lower jaw is lifted. There is no history or evidence of cervical injury. Which basic maneuver is appropriate to open the airway?

  1. Pressure directly onto the larynx to close it
  2. Forceful flexion of the neck
  3. Blind sweeping of the mouth with a finger
  4. Insertion of a rigid object between the teeth
  5. Head tilt with chin lift
Answer and explanation

Head tilt with chin lift

In the absence of suspected cervical injury, this maneuver lifts the tongue away from the posterior pharynx.

Option explanations

Head tilt with chin lift: In the absence of suspected cervical injury, this maneuver lifts the tongue away from the posterior pharynx.

Pressure directly onto the larynx to close it: Closing the airway is not an opening maneuver.

Forceful flexion of the neck: Flexion does not provide the usual airway-opening position.

Blind sweeping of the mouth with a finger: This is not indicated without a visible removable object and can push material deeper.

Insertion of a rigid object between the teeth: Improvised objects can injure tissues and do not reliably maintain the airway.
